evidence.claim: The General Assembly demanded that Russia immediately cease its unlawful use of force against Ukraine, withdraw all military forces, and pursue a peaceful resolution through political dialogue, negotiations, mediation, and other peaceful means while protecting civilians.
evidence.title: UN General Assembly adopts resolution on Ukraine, 2 March 2022
evidence.excerpt: The General Assembly demanded that Russia immediately cease its unlawful use of force against Ukraine, withdraw all military forces, and pursue a peaceful resolution through political dialogue, negotiations, mediation, and other peaceful means while protecting civilians.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN record of the resolution and its peace/humanitarian language.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and provides the legal-diplomatic frame for Thailand's supportive vote and later abstentions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is UN context rather than Prayut-specific conduct, but it anchors the decision Thailand was responding to.
contrary_evidence: The press record is not Thailand-specific and does not by itself establish Thai attribution.

evidence.claim: After Thai fighters were scrambled in response to a Myanmar combat aircraft briefly entering Thai airspace, Prayut Chan-o-cha said the incident was 'not a big deal' and noted that a Myanmar defense attache had apologized.
evidence.title: Thailand scrambles fighters after Myanmar jet airspace breach
evidence.excerpt: After Thai fighters were scrambled in response to a Myanmar combat aircraft briefly entering Thai airspace, Prayut Chan-o-cha said the incident was 'not a big deal' and noted that a Myanmar defense attache had apologized.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with a direct Prayut quote and clear border-security context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to a cross-border security episode involving a neighboring conflict.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's public handling of the border incident, though the underlying military response was carried out by Thai air force and defense officials.
contrary_evidence: Thailand still deployed fighters, so the episode was not purely verbal de-escalation.

evidence.claim: Thailand hosted junta ministers and other Southeast Asian officials for informal Myanmar talks aimed at a diplomatic path toward normalcy and the five-point peace process, but the meeting drew criticism from ASEAN actors who said it risked breaching the bloc's exclusion of junta representatives.
evidence.title: Myanmar shadow govt raises alarm after junta meets ASEAN members
evidence.excerpt: Thailand hosted junta ministers and other Southeast Asian officials for informal Myanmar talks aimed at a diplomatic path toward normalcy and the five-point peace process, but the meeting drew criticism from ASEAN actors who said it risked breaching the bloc's exclusion of junta representatives.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with both the host government's framing and the main contrary criticism.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to Thailand's regional conflict mediation posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Thailand's foreign ministry and government hosting role, not to Prayut personally ordering a military operation.
contrary_evidence: Several ASEAN members skipped the meeting and critics said it was not helpful and could breach ASEAN policy on junta representation.

evidence.claim: Thailand abstained on the UN resolution condemning Russia's annexation of Ukrainian territory while the Thai foreign ministry said Thailand still upheld the UN Charter, sovereignty, territorial integrity, and opposition to the use of force.
evidence.title: Thai PBS report on Thailand abstaining on Ukraine annexation resolution
evidence.excerpt: Thailand abstained on the UN resolution condemning Russia's annexation of Ukrainian territory while the Thai foreign ministry said Thailand still upheld the UN Charter, sovereignty, territorial integrity, and opposition to the use of force.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and numbered explanation in article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Thai-language independent reporting of the government's stated rationale, contemporaneous with the vote.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to Thailand's Ukraine policy stance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Thai foreign ministry under Prayut's government; not an individual military order.
contrary_evidence: The abstention reduced the force of Thailand's public opposition to annexation compared with a yes vote.

evidence.claim: Thailand abstained on a resolution creating a register of damage from the war in Ukraine; the UN text said Russia must be held to account for violations of international law and the need for a reparations mechanism.
evidence.title: General Assembly Adopts Text Recommending Creation of Register to Document Damages Caused by Russian Federation Aggression against Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Thailand abstained on a resolution creating a register of damage from the war in Ukraine; the UN text said Russia must be held to account for violations of international law and the need for a reparations mechanism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN meeting record with the vote and accountability framing; directly contemporaneous.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to Thailand's accountability posture on the Ukraine war.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Thailand's government and UN delegation under Prayut's cabinet.
contrary_evidence: Thailand's abstention again fell short of a clear pro-accountability vote.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice, escalation, or crisis-management episode is shown.
Command-and-control, custody, and safety-governance evidence tied specifically to Prayut remains thin.
PM-level attribution for 2022 international-security choices is still thin; most evidence is ministry or delegation posture.
The Myanmar and Ukraine material does not yet show concrete peace or accountability outcomes attributable to Prayut.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for the APEC crackdown and the deep-south emergency regime remains limited.
The torture/disappearance law is an important reform, but year-end enforcement evidence is still weak.
Direct evidence on the sponsors and mechanism of the election-system change is still thin.
4B.4 and 4B.7 remain under-evidenced relative to the stronger protest, media, and term-limit material.
Budget intent and macro recovery are better evidenced than actual implementation and take-up.
Evidence on appointments, anti-capture, and mistake-correction is still weak.
Direct service-delivery, take-up, and quality evidence is thin outside budget allocations and national surveys.
Ruler-specific causal attribution for rural, child, and mental-health outcomes remains weak.
No independent 2022 finding of personal lying, self-dealing, or concealed conflict of interest is shown.
The package relies too much on allegations, self-defense, and broader regime context.
The program basis is only partly explicit; some objectives are inferred from budgets and coalition moves rather than a single frozen program statement.
Outcome evidence is sectoral and mixed, and external reopening effects remain hard to separate from ruler skill.
